title: The SI System: Seven Base Units
subject: Physics
objective: In 1999 NASA lost the Mars Climate Orbiter because one team used pound-force and another newtons. Why the world uses one system, the SI, built on seven base units.

fill.q: The SI unit of electric current is the ____.
The SI unit of amount of substance is the ____.
The SI unit of luminous intensity is the ____.

tf.q: The kilogram is a base unit.
tf.explain: Mass is a base quantity; its unit is the kilogram.

tf.q: The newton is a base unit.
tf.explain: It is derived: kg m s⁻².

tf.q: Degree Celsius is the SI base unit of temperature.
tf.explain: The base unit is the kelvin.

ar.a: Every unit in mechanics can be written using kg, m and s.
ar.r: Mechanical units are derived from mass, length and time.

ar.a: The SI is used worldwide in science.
ar.r: One common system avoids costly unit errors.

num.q: Express the joule in base units.

steps: Pa = N / m² = kg m s⁻² / m²

short.q: Name the seven SI base quantities with their units and symbols.
short.solution: Length metre m; mass kilogram kg; time second s; electric current ampere A; temperature kelvin K; amount of substance mole mol; luminous intensity candela cd.

match.explain: Each unit matches its base quantity.
